topic.title: How a melted candy bar beside a radar tube led to the microwave oven

title: How Did a Melted Candy Bar Invent the Microwave?
description:
How did a melted candy bar give us the microwave oven?
Percy Spencer, a Raytheon engineer, was testing a radar tube when the chocolate in his pocket melted. We build the tube in 3D and show how it heats your food.
Sources: History.com (Jan 1947).
Animations are simplified illustrations, not exact to scale.
cta: Which invention should we take apart next? Comment

topic.title: How Hoover Dam turns the push of Lake Mead into electricity, and why a lower lake cuts it

title: Why Does Hoover Dam Need Lake Mead to Be Full?
description:
Why does Hoover Dam need Lake Mead to be full?
We cut the dam open in 3D: the intake towers, the pipes, the turbine and the spinning magnets, and why the height of Lake Mead decides how much power it makes.
Sources: US Bureau of Reclamation (May 2026).
Animations are simplified illustrations, not exact to scale.

topic.title: How the first transistor, two gold contacts on a plastic wedge at Bell Labs, became the switch inside every chip

title: What Did the First Transistor Actually Look Like?
description:
What did the first transistor actually look like?
At Bell Labs in December 1947, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain pressed two gold contacts onto a piece of germanium. We build it in 3D, show how it amplifies, then dive into a modern graphics chip built from the same switch.
Sources: Computer History Museum, NVIDIA GeForce News (Sep 2022).
Animations are simplified illustrations, not exact to scale.
